content.overview: A root-zone steering report should show the baseline, intervention, measured response, uncertainty, acceptance criteria and next authorized action so another qualified person can reconstruct what changed and whether it worked.

vocabulary.definition: The measured pre-change state used for comparison.
Predefined evidence required to consider a steering intervention acceptable for its intended purpose.
A predefined condition requiring the intervention to be stopped, reversed or escalated.

sections.title: Document the intervention precisely
sections.body: Record zone, crop stage, media, event volume/frequency, input chemistry, environmental context and timestamps so the change is reproducible.

sections.title: Compare like with like
sections.body: Use the same measurement method and representative positions before and after the intervention. Changing sensor placement or sampling method can invalidate the comparison.

sections.title: Escalate when response conflicts with the model
sections.body: Unexpected water-content, EC or crop-response trends should reopen the hypothesis rather than be forced into the intended steering narrative.

workedExamples: A steering trial intended to reduce overnight saturation instead produces rising root-zone EC and uneven dryback; the report should flag the adverse response and trigger review rather than call the schedule successful.
commonMistakes: Documenting only the schedule and not the response.
Ignoring adverse evidence because the intervention was planned.
content.practicalApplication: Write a steering verification report from a supplied baseline/intervention dataset with acceptance and reversal criteria.
content.summary: Advanced steering is defensible only when the intervention and measured response are both reconstructable.
